newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber quietly steady at close.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber quietly steady at close.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed steady after a quiet session, with sentiment aided by gains in Tokyo and recent buying from China, dealers said.
Trading was quiet as most dealers are making their way to Kuala Lumpur for the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) annual dinner on Friday.
"A higher Tokyo market and small purchases by China in recent days are helping sentiment," a dealer said. "Trading was almost at a standstill as players are heading for the dinner."
Volume was thin with most business confined to hand-to-mouth basis, dealers said.
"Recent rains could have also caused producers to hold back their stocks," another dealer said. "The market could expect some tight supply in short-term because of weather factors."
Traders offered SMR 20 at 304 cents, SMR10 at 305, SMR 5 at 316, SMR L at 341, SMR CV at 361 and drum latex at 232.
November RSS Ones buyer ended unchanged at 308.50 cents ($1.23) a kg while November SMR 20 was up half cent at 306.50.
The INRO five-day moving average was 238.93 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 23 from 238.91 on Oct 22. The daily indicator price was 238.96 against 238.95.
